note: Crafts of The Unmade/The Making (destruction_creation axis). RUINWORK is the destruction-pole craft of the Unmakers — who hold that ending a thing WELL is a craft, and that the world is choked with what should have ended; MAKECRAFT is the creation-pole craft of the Wrights of the New, who cannot stop making and whose cities are never finished, which is the point. Neither is villainous: an Unmaker's clearing is a mercy and a Wright's ceaselessness is a waste. Authored by Aevi, SNG-054.

abilities.name: Ruinwork
abilities.narrationHints: It comes down the way he said it would, exactly where he said, and nothing else is touched.
abilities.description: The destruction-pole mastery: ending things well. Not violence — DEMOLITION, with an ethic: what should end, ends cleanly, and what should stand is left standing.
abilities.notFor: Ending what should stand (the Unmakers' whole discipline is that line); making; anything that requires patience with a dead thing.

tree.name: The Fault Line
tree.grants: See exactly where a thing wants to break — a wall, a plan, an alliance, an argument.
tree.cannot: Seeing the fault is not being right that it should be broken.

tree.name: The Clean Break
tree.grants: Break precisely at the fault — the thing comes apart where you chose and nowhere else.
tree.cannot: Precise is not reversible. A clean break is still a break.

tree.name: The Good Ending
tree.grants: End a thing WELL — a building, an institution, a life's work, a war — so that what it was is honored and what comes after is not poisoned by how it went.
tree.cannot: You must be right that it should end. The Unmakers' cult, the Scouring, is what this becomes when that judgment stops being made.

bounds.text: WHAT YOU END TO SUSTAIN YOURSELF, YOU HAVE ENDED — it does not come back when the hard stretch does

abilities.plainly: A endurance/hardship/psychological action that strengthens someone. Its strength is rated 4 out of 10 It affects 1 target, and lasts for about a day Ranks: rank 2 deepens upkeepRelief; rank 3 extends targets. Limit: what You End TO Sustain Yourself, You Have Ended — it does not come back when the hard stretch does.

abilities.name: The Undoing Word
abilities.narrationHints: You speak the undoing of one thing — not destroy it, UNMAKE it, so that it does not fall or burn but simply stops having been assembled, and is only its parts again.
abilities.description: The Unmaker art of the undoing — returning a made or bound thing to its unassembled state, so it is not destroyed but un-done, its making reversed. The clean art of those who end things properly.
abilities.notFor: It unmakes the assembled, not the living or the truly singular — you cannot unmake a person, a soul, a genuine unity. And unmaking is not free of grief just because it is clean; a thing un-done is still gone.

tree.name: The Undoing Word
tree.grants: Unmake an assembled thing back to its unbound parts, reversing its making.
tree.cannot: It cannot touch the living or the singular, it costs dearly, and un-done is still gone — cleanness is not the same as no loss.

tree.name: The Longer Unmaking
tree.grants: The word reaches what is BOUND as well as what is built — a working, a ward, a seal, a pact held by craft rather than by will. And the scale rises: not a thing but an assembly, a mechanism, a gate, the whole of something that was put together.
tree.cannot: Still never the living, never the truly singular. Unmaking a binding releases whatever that binding held, and the GM decides what that was. And the cost climbs with the scale — Unmakers who reach too far come apart along the seams they opened.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: the word reaches WHAT IS BOUND as well as what is BUILT — a working, a ward, a seal, A PACT held by craft. Unmaking bindings rather than objects is the T-IV kind-change.

intensity.conserve: unmake a small assembly — half the reach, and the parts survive
intensity.surge: double it; unmaking a binding is unmaking whatever the binding was holding

bounds.text: IT CANNOT TOUCH THE LIVING OR THE SINGULAR
it costs DEARLY
unmaking a binding is unmaking WHATEVER THE BINDING WAS HOLDING

abilities.plainly: A fight action that deals damage. It rolls 4d6+2 across a scope of 3 Ranks: rank 2 adds to special. Limit: iT Cannot Touch The Living OR The Singular.

abilities.name: The Last Unmaking
abilities.narrationHints: You unmake something that was never supposed to be unmakeable — a bound working, an ancient pact, a thing the world had decided was permanent — and the world, briefly, has to agree it was wrong.
abilities.description: The Unmaker capstone — the undoing of a thing meant to be permanent, a working or bond the world held as fixed. The deepest and most feared Unmaker gift, because some things were made permanent for good reason.
abilities.notFor: One permanent thing, once, at enormous cost — and the world resists; unmaking the fixed takes everything and cannot be repeated soon. And you do not always know WHY a thing was made permanent until you have unmade it.

tree.name: The Last Unmaking
tree.grants: Unmake a thing meant to be permanent — a fixed working, an ancient bond.
tree.cannot: It costs nearly all you have, the world resists the unmaking of the fixed, and some things were sealed for reasons you learn only after you have broken the seal.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: UNMAKE A THING MEANT TO BE PERMANENT — a fixed working, an ancient bond. The capstone is a KIND (ending what was made to never end) at near-total cost, AND THE WORLD RESISTS IT.

intensity.conserve: REFUSED — there is no partial unmaking of a permanent thing; it holds or it does not.
intensity.surge: REFUSED — it already costs nearly all you have and the world is already resisting.

bounds.text: it costs your whole remaining energy pool and leaves you at zero, unable to use any craft until you rest a full night
THE WORLD RESISTS THE UNMAKING OF PERMANENT THINGS

abilities.plainly: A fight action that deals damage. It rolls 5d6+6 across a scope of 4 Limit: iT Costs Nearly All You Have.

abilities.name: The True Making
abilities.narrationHints: You make the thing properly — not quickly, not cleverly, but TRULY, so that it is exactly what it should be and will hold because it was made right the first time.
abilities.description: The Wright art of true making — building a thing correctly and completely, so it is sound to its core and endures because nothing in it was cut short. The maker's first real mastery: not fast, but right.
abilities.notFor: It makes sound things, not living or magical ones — a true making is still a made thing. And making truly costs time and care; you cannot rush a true making and have it stay true.

tree.name: The True Making
tree.grants: Make a thing truly and completely, sound to its core and enduring.
tree.cannot: It makes the made, not the living; it cannot be hurried without ceasing to be true; and a thing made right outlasts its maker, with all that carries.

tree.name: The Sound Repair
tree.grants: Bring a made thing back to true rather than merely patching it — find where the making was cut short or has failed, and remake that part as it should have been. A true repair is not a seam; the thing is sound again to its core.
tree.cannot: It repairs the made, never the living; it needs enough of the original left to read the maker's intent; and a true repair takes the same care the true making did — you cannot hurry it either.

tree.name: The Work That Outlasts
tree.grants: Make at scale and for time — a hall, a bridge, a road built so completely that generations use it without knowing your name. Your makings resist decay, ill-use, and weather beyond what their materials should allow, and another Wright can read the trueness in your work and learn from it.
tree.cannot: Scale multiplies the time and care, never reduces it; a thing made right outlasts its maker, with all that carries; and the Wrights hold that what endures is judged by what it was FOR — the GM prices a great making by what it serves.

rankDeltas.delta: bring a made thing BACK TO TRUE rather than patching — find where the making was CUT SHORT and finish it
make AT SCALE AND FOR TIME — a hall, a bridge, a road built so completely that GENERATIONS use it without knowing your name

intensity.conserve: make it sound — half the scope, and it is finished today
intensity.surge: double it; SCALE MULTIPLIES THE TIME AND CARE, NEVER REDUCES IT

bounds.text: IT MAKES THE MADE, NOT THE LIVING
IT CANNOT BE HURRIED without ceasing to be true making
SCALE MULTIPLIES THE TIME AND CARE, NEVER REDUCES IT

abilities.plainly: A create action that makes or animates something. Its strength is rated 6 out of 10 across a scope of 3, and lasts for about 12 months Ranks: rank 2 deepens quality; rank 3 extends scope. Limit: iT Makes The Made, Not The Living.

abilities.name: The Reforging
abilities.narrationHints: You take the broken thing and do not merely mend it — you reforge it, so that where it broke is now where it is strongest, the break itself made into the making.
abilities.description: The Wright art of reforging — remaking a broken thing so that its breaking becomes its strength, the flaw worked into a truer form. The deep gift of makers who know that broken is not the same as ruined.
abilities.notFor: It reforges the made, not the living — a broken bone or a broken heart is not a Wright's work. And reforging asks the thing be truly broken first; you cannot reforge what has only been scratched.

tree.name: The Reforging
tree.grants: Reforge a broken thing so its break becomes its strength.
tree.cannot: It works on the made, not the living; it needs a true break to work with; and the reforged thing is changed — stronger, but no longer the thing it was before it broke.

tree.name: The Deep Reforging
tree.grants: Work breaks that should be past working — a thing shattered rather than cracked, a thing broken many times over, a thing broken so long ago its maker is forgotten. The reforged piece carries every break as a line of strength, and a Wright who reads it can recite the whole history from the metal.
tree.cannot: Still the made, never the living. The more breaks worked in, the further the thing travels from what it was — at some point it is a new thing wearing an old name, and the Wrights argue about where that point falls. And a reforging this deep takes days, not hours.

mechanic.note: T-IV. 'Reforge a broken thing so ITS BREAK BECOMES ITS STRENGTH.'

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: work breaks THAT SHOULD BE PAST WORKING — a thing shattered rather than cracked, broken many times over. The more breaks worked in, the more the thing becomes ABOUT its breaking.

intensity.conserve: mend the break — half the transformation, and it is simply repaired
intensity.surge: double it; THE MORE BREAKS WORKED IN, THE MORE THE THING BECOMES ABOUT ITS BREAKING

bounds.text: IT WORKS ON THE MADE, NOT THE LIVING
IT NEEDS A TRUE BREAK to work — an undamaged thing offers nothing
the more breaks worked in, THE MORE THE THING BECOMES ABOUT ITS BREAKING

abilities.plainly: A create action that makes or animates something. Its strength is rated 7 out of 10, and lasts for about 12 months Ranks: rank 2 adds to special. Limit: iT Works ON The Made, Not The Living.

abilities.name: The Masterwork
abilities.narrationHints: You make the one thing — the work that holds everything you have ever learned about making, so complete and so right that it will teach the next maker who studies it long after you are gone.
abilities.description: The Wright capstone — the masterwork, the single making that gathers a lifetime's craft into one true thing, sound enough to teach across generations. The maker's greatest gift and their legacy both: to make a thing that outlasts and instructs.
abilities.notFor: One masterwork, once, over real time and enormous cost — it is not produced in a beat but committed to; and a masterwork, once made, is a fact and a teacher in the world. It cannot be casually surpassed, even by you.

tree.name: The Masterwork
tree.grants: Make a single masterwork that gathers a lifetime's craft into one enduring, teaching thing.
tree.cannot: It demands real time and nearly all you have, it stands as a permanent fact and teacher, and you may never make its equal again — a masterwork is, often, the making you are measured by ever after.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: make a SINGLE MASTERWORK that gathers a lifetime's craft into ONE ENDURING, TEACHING THING. The capstone is a KIND (a work that teaches after you) at near-total cost.

intensity.conserve: REFUSED — a half-made masterwork is an unfinished work, and the Wrights are unsentimental about those.
intensity.surge: REFUSED — it already demands nearly all you have.

bounds.text: IT DEMANDS REAL TIME AND NEARLY ALL YOU HAVE
IT STANDS AS A PROMISE you must then live up to

abilities.plainly: A create action that makes or animates something. Its strength is rated 9 out of 10 across a scope of 4, and lasts for about 122 months Limit: iT Demands Real Time And Nearly All You Have.

abilities.name: The Last Fault
abilities.narrationHints: Everything has a fault. They have been looking at yours since you sat down.
abilities.description: ⚠️ THE LAST ONES' CRAFT, and the tradition's own capstone problem made explicit. Unmaking finds the fault in a thing and opens it. A PERSON IS A THING WITH A FAULT. The Enders-Well hold this should be reserved for what should end; the Last Ones hold that the fault is reason enough.
abilities.notFor: Anything faultless, which is nothing. ⚠️ NOT SELECTIVE — you open the fault you found, not the one you wanted, so a Last One aiming at a leg sometimes gets a life. And it CANNOT BE STOPPED PARTWAY.

tree.name: The Last Fault
tree.grants: Find the fault in a living thing and BREAK it open. What follows follows the fault, not your intent.
tree.cannot: Choosing what the fault does. Anything already ended.

tree.name: The Whole Fault
tree.grants: BREAK every fault at once. Nothing about this rank is careful and the tradition says so plainly.
tree.cannot: Stopping. Bystanders — the faults nearest yours break too.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ HIGHEST variance in the catalog — the fault decides, not the wielder.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: every fault at once, and the faults NEAREST YOURS break too

intensity.conserve: one fault, opened a little — half, and it can be closed again
intensity.surge: the whole fault; THE FAULTS NEAREST YOURS BREAK TOO

bounds.text: NOT SELECTIVE — you open the fault you FOUND, not the one you wanted
IT CANNOT BE STOPPED PARTWAY
AT r2 THE FAULTS NEAREST YOURS BREAK TOO — INCLUDING YOURS

abilities.plainly: A fight attack dealing 5d6 with the highest damage variance in the game, because you do not control what the fault does when it opens. You cannot choose the effect and you cannot stop it partway. At rank 2 it also hits others near the target, including you. Everything living has a fault, so nothing is immune.

abilities.name: The Found Fault
abilities.narrationHints: Everything made has a fault in it — the place it will go when it goes. You find that place and you put one small, precise, entirely sufficient force there. The Unmakers consider inelegant demolition a moral failing.
abilities.description: The Unmakers' first offense: the smallest correct action. Not power, placement.
abilities.notFor: Anything with no fault to find — the genuinely whole, the newly made, the perfectly kept; brute force (if it takes more than one placement you have misread it); working blind; putting it back.

tree.name: The One Place
tree.grants: Find the fault in a made thing on or around a target — a shield's grain, a helm's seam, a joist, a buckle, the flaw in the stone they are standing on — and open it. What was holding stops holding, onto them.
tree.cannot: MADE OR FLAWED THINGS — a whole, new, well-kept object gives you very little, and living bodies only where they are already hurt. You must perceive the fault; guessing wastes the placement.

tree.name: The Clean Break
tree.grants: Take the fault that matters rather than the nearest one — the load-bearing member, the keystone, the axle. Structures come down where you decide they come down.
tree.cannot: ⚠ A STRUCTURE COMES DOWN ON WHAT IS UNDER IT: allies in the area are struck ONE RUNG LOWER. You choose where it falls, not who is there.

tree.name: The Beautiful Ruin
tree.grants: A whole made thing, opened at every fault at once, in the order that brings it down best. Halls, gates, bridges, engines, and the people relying on them.
tree.cannot: ⚠ THE WIELDER IS STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER if inside the ruin, and it CANNOT BE PUT BACK — the Unmakers hold you answerable for what you cleared and whether it should have been. The Scouring do this for its own sake.

intensity.conserve: open one small fault
intensity.surge: the beautiful ruin; IT CANNOT BE PUT BACK and you are answerable

bounds.text: MADE OR FLAWED THINGS — the whole and well-kept give little
you must PERCEIVE the fault; guessing wastes it
ALLIES UNDER A FALLING STRUCTURE ARE STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER
it CANNOT BE PUT BACK

abilities.plainly: A fight/puzzle action that opens the fault in a made thing onto a target. Rated 7 of 10 across a scope of 2. Limit: it needs a fault to find.

abilities.name: The Sudden Work
abilities.narrationHints: You make something. Here, now, fast, and in the space a person is currently occupying. A spar through the gap in their guard; a wall closing where they were going to be; a bracket around a limb. The Wrights do not fight so much as build inconveniently.
abilities.description: The Wrights' first offense: creation used as an attack, which the Wrights find slightly embarrassing and are very good at.
abilities.notFor: Making from nothing — there must be material to hand (stone, timber, iron, wreckage, the building you are in); delicacy; unmaking what you built (that is the Unmakers' craft, and yours stays); anything faster than the material allows.

tree.name: The Driven Spar
tree.grants: Take material to hand and make it FAST, into them — a spar through a guard, a spike out of the floor, an iron bracket that closes on an arm. Crude, immediate, and it stays there afterward.
tree.cannot: MATERIAL MUST BE PRESENT — bare ground and no wreckage gives you nothing. What you make REMAINS, in them or in the room, and you cannot unmake it.

tree.name: The Raised Work
tree.grants: Build at scale in the middle of the fight — a wall across a charge, a cage, a collapsing scaffold over a line of them.
tree.cannot: ⚠ WHAT YOU RAISE IS IN EVERYONE'S WAY: allies in the area are struck ONE RUNG LOWER or cut off by your own work. It stays up until someone takes it down.

tree.name: The Thing That Was Not There
tree.grants: A whole work, at speed, where people are standing. It is finished before they understand it is being built, and they are inside it.
tree.cannot: ⚠ THE WIELDER IS STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER if inside their own work, and it REMAINS AFTERWARD — a permanent structure on the site of your fight, which the Ceaseless would call a good day and the valley may not.

intensity.conserve: drive one spar
intensity.surge: the whole work; IT REMAINS AFTERWARD and you cannot unmake it

WHAT YOU MAKE REMAINS — you cannot unmake it
ALLIES ARE STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER or cut off by your own work
at rank 3 the wielder is struck one rung lower if inside it

abilities.plainly: A fight/puzzle action that builds something violently into the space a target occupies. Rated 7 of 10 across a scope of 2. Limit: material must be present, and what you make remains.
